title: Bengali-Spiced Tomato Chutney
summary: Chunky tomatoes cooked down with crackling cumin, mustard and fennel seeds, ginger, chilli, cider vinegar and brown sugar into a sweet, sour and spicy relish.

ingredients.item: ripe plum tomatoes, cored and cut in 1 cm pieces
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Temper the spices
steps.text: Heat the oil in the pan over a medium-high heat. Add the cumin and mustard seeds and, as soon as the mustard seeds crackle, a few seconds later, add the fennel seeds. Have the tomatoes ready, as the seeds burn quickly.

steps.title: Add everything else
steps.text: Tip in the tomatoes, ginger, garlic, green chilli, vinegar, sugar, chilli flakes, salt and bay leaf, and bring to the boil.

steps.title: Reduce
steps.text: Simmer uncovered for 40-50 minutes, stirring now and then and more often as it thickens. Halfway through, lightly mash about half the tomatoes so the chutney is part jammy, part chunky.

steps.title: Check the set
steps.text: It is ready when glossy and a spatula drawn across the base leaves a clear path for a few seconds. It will firm up more as it cools.

steps.title: Jar
steps.text: Spoon into clean, hot jars with the bay leaf on top, seal and cool.

tips: Have all the tomatoes chopped before heating the oil, as the seeds take only seconds to toast.
A frequent mistake is covering the pan; the chutney needs to stay uncovered so the liquid can evaporate.
Ripe summer plum tomatoes give the best colour; good tinned plum tomatoes also work out of season.
Adjust the chilli flakes up or down to taste before jarring.
storage: Keep in sealed jars in the fridge for up to 1 month. It can be frozen for up to 6 months. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
